title: 1981-04-16_Pat_81.txt
concise_summary: PKD develops a systematic theological explanation of his 2-3-74 religious experience through the metaphor of a mediator-redeemer acting as a 'two-way lens' between alienated human consciousness and an incomprehensible external world. Drawing on Gnostic ontology, Christian soteriology, Platonic eidos, and Plotinian emanation, he argues that reality normally appears as impenetrable foreign language, but through the Holy Spirit's mediation (identified with the Logos and Christ), world and self become unified and comprehensible—a state he claims has no antecedent in religious interpretation. He further theorizes that objects themselves are linguistic signs, and that an invisible latent realm coaxial with the physical world communicates via modulated information patterns, establishing his core axiom: 'some mind or minds is/are using the physical universe as a carrier for a purely informational world.'
key_claims: Reality perceived directly is totally closed, foreign, and ambiguous, allusive but unclarifying—its language is foreign or obscure to human consciousness
Salvation consists in the appearance of a mediator-redeemer (Christ/Holy Spirit) that acts as a two-way lens, unifying the normally disjunctive conditions of subject and world
The Holy Spirit's gift of 'universal language' reverses the Fall's atomization of unity into plurality, restoring comprehension between self and world—this is what PKD experienced on 2-3-74

Objects are not merely material things but encoded linguistic messages; recognizing this semiotic status triggered PKD's generalized realization that 'things (non-verbal things, i.e. objects) were language'
There exists a latent invisible realm coaxial with and modulating the physical universe, knowable only through information-traffic patterns, not geographic space-time coordinates

The entire Bible, especially the Gospels and Acts, functions as a 'music' whose 'groove' is our modulated physical reality—reading scripture is extracting the divine information-structure from the carrier wave of material existence

tensions: PKD cannot explain HOW or WHY the two conditions (salvation vs. normal alienation) arose, only that they exist as fact—epistemological impasse acknowledging limits of his insight
Paradox of the solution: each statement within salvation's clarified condition addresses only itself, not the total situation—the decoded cypher doesn't explain the whole system
Uncertainty whether VALIS experienced was internal (in mind) or external (in world) or both—the boundaries between inner and outer collapse but remain conceptually unclear
Tension between simultaneity and alternation: latent realm is simultaneous with, not alternate to, physical reality (thus not alternate-world science fiction but coaxial existence)
Discrepancy in PKD's knowledge: 'I seem to know how but not who' solved the problem, and 'I do not know why' it occurred—partial comprehension mixed with fundamental ignorance
Cannot voluntarily cause the salvation state to return—it departed 'as mysteriously as it came,' suggesting external agency beyond PKD's control
The girl did not explicitly say 'secret' or 'illegal'—PKD retrospectively realizes he 'knew' these meanings only in the moment, raising questions about memory, projection, or genuine revelation

Unclear whether PKD's simultaneous perception of VALIS 'in my mind + externally in world' is metaphorical or literal—the collapse of inner/outer distinction may reflect psychological rather than ontological fact
The claim that his interpretation of religious experience 'has no antecedent in the history of human interpretation' is historically unverifiable and likely hyperbolic
Steganographic identification of 'Jesus' = 'Zeus Zagreus' is presented without etymological or philological argument—appears intuitive rather than scholarly
The assertion that Eucharist derives solely from Dionysian mystery cult (not Judaism) contradicts mainstream scholarship and appears idiosyncratic
PKD's 'Ditheon' concept (two selves: individual consciousness + impersonal Atman) is introduced fragmentarily and cuts off mid-sentence, leaving the full theory incomplete
The meta-abstraction concept is invoked repeatedly but never fully defined—it remains a placeholder for an unnamed cognitive operation
Binary rest-motion system for information registration is asserted but not explained mechanically
The notion that 'modulation' and 'perturbation' refer to 'the same thing' is stated but not justified
